text:
kevin: Heads up — hit a production incident last night. Console queries spiked and authz calls to the capability service started timing out. UI began showing partial dashboards with 'restricted' overlays instead of a clear error. We need to decide on an architecture for graceful degradation: prioritize latency availability vs strict auth correctness?

maria: Saw it. The auth service p99 jumped; front-end treated 503s from auth as 'no data' which made it look like blank dashboards, super confusing.

siva: Short-term: we should add an auth-cache fallback in the console proxy. If downstream auth is slow, consult a cached subject->perm map for N seconds and tag the response as stale.

jules: Be careful — cached permissions can leak. We should allow cached grants only for read-only surfaces and only if we have a valid TTL for that grant.

kevin: Sketch proposal: per-route degradation modes: strict (block), read-cache (serve with cached perms), allowlist (serve only whitelisted metrics). Default = strict. Low-sensitivity dashboards can opt into read-cache.

maria: Example config idea:
```
degradation:
  routes:
    /dashboards/*:
      mode: readcache
      cache_ttl: 30s
      audit_flag: true
    /admin/*:
      mode: strict
```

siva: Implementation note: console query layer should talk to an auth sidecar that returns three states: ALLOW, DENY, UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN triggers the degradation policy lookup; if route permits, we consult local cache or allowlist.

ops-bot: ALERT: during incident auth-service p99 = 2.5s, error rate spiked. Runbook: ops/runbooks/auth-service-timeout.md (link) :warning:

jules: Telemetry must include an "auth_degraded" tag and a token-hash for postmortem correlation. Also, auto-disable read-cache if >0.1% of queries used fallback for tenants marked 'sensitive'.

maria: Also: populate caches proactively on deploys / warmup so we don't rely on cold-cache during a traffic spike.

kevin: Action items: (1) RFC for "auth degradation lanes" (owner: kevin) (2) prototype spike-safe auth-cache in console proxy (owner: siva) (3) add audit tag + token-hash to telemetry (owner: maria) (4) simulate load tests for false-allow and latency improvement (owner: jules). Target: RFC by end of next week.

siva: I'll prototype a sidecar change and open a PR by Thu. Tests: cache hit ratio, false-allow rate (must be <= 0.001%), end-to-end query latency improvement.

jules: +1. Also propose a longer-term path: precomputed snapshot responses for heavy dashboards so we can serve stale-but-safe content during downstream outages.

kevin: Thanks everyone. Tagging @maria @siva @jules — moving the design to an RFC thread. :thumbsup:
